newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms amid ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms amid ample liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in moderate late trading on Tuesday despite an easing in money market liquidity, dealers said.
They said the liquidity-driven market was very briefly rattled by sudden sharp declines in the stock market due to unfounded health rumours linked to Indonesia's Vice President.
Vice-President Try Sutrisno was scheduled to attend a fast-breaking meal with senior government officials later on Tuesday, an official from the vice-president's office said.
Currency dealers said the unfounded rumours had circulated in the stock market since late-morning but failed to affect the foreign exchange market.
"There was basically no follow-through in the forex market until late afternoon as some Singapore players made some buying but this was immediately countered by local players," one said.
He said the market was relatively calm and focused further on liquidity anticipation.
Some dealers said the small dollar rise was partly due to a surprise turnaround in money market liquidity in the afternoon after the central bank offered repo possibility on Tuesday.
Dealers said the 300-billion rupiah one-week SBIs repo seemed to have helped ease initial liquidity worry.
Overnight rupiah fell to eight percent in the afternoon from an early high of 19.0/20.0 percent.
Spot rupiah briefly touched a low of 2,375.0 in the late afternoon after the central bank raised its fixing, but bounced back quickly to 2,374.0/75.0 at 0930 GMT.
Spot opened at 2,373.0/74.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,372.70/73.00 and 2,370.75/71.25, respectively.
Overnight swaps were last at 1.0/1.1. Tom.next swaps fell to 0.55/0.60 from an early high of 1.2/1.4 points.
Dealers said swap rates fell across the board as liquidity eased, helping calm operators despite the underlying worry over a possible surge in rupiah demand ahead of the festivities.
The foreign exchange market will be closed for Eid al-Fitr on February 10 and 11 and reopen on February 12, while the stock market will be closed from February 7 to 11 inclusive.
Dealers said the dollar came under some pressure earlier as operators established short dollar positions to catch weekend premiums when they covered back on Thursday.
One-month swaps declined to 13.25/14.00 from 14.0/15.0, two to 26.75/28.00 from 28.0/29.5, three to 38.5/39.5 from 40.0/41.5 and six to 78.25/79.50 from 78.0/81.0 points.
The bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,373/2,565 and the conversion band at 2,373/2,421 on Tuesday, the first depreciation this week.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by three points last week after lowering it by two points the previous week.
